documents.title: Micrographic surgery report
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group - micrographic surgery
Date of procedure: 01/26/2022
Patient: Eugene Connolly, 67 M
Diagnosis: basal cell carcinoma, nodular, lateral nose (biopsy 12/13/2021).
Anticoagulation: warfarin continued, INR 2.4 two weeks ago.
Allergies: NKDA.

Procedure: Margin-controlled micrographic excision under local anesthesia. Stage 1 showed residual tumor at one peripheral margin; stage 2 cleared. Final defect repaired with a local nasal flap. Estimated blood loss minimal; hemostasis with electrocautery. Pressure dressing.

Result: margins clear after 2 stages.
Plan: suture removal in 1 week. Acetaminophen for discomfort. Annual full skin exam here.
Copy to primary care.

Outside gastroenterology practice
Visit: 06/20/2022
Re: Eugene Connolly, 67 y/o man

Reason for referral: dysphagia.

History: Mr. Connolly describes six months of steadily worsening difficulty getting both solids and liquids down. He has nighttime regurgitation of food that is clearly undigested, which sets off coughing spells. He is also bothered by halitosis despite careful oral hygiene. He has diabetes with neuropathy, hypertension, and atrial fibrillation on warfarin; a nasal basal cell carcinoma was excised in January.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin, atorvastatin 40 mg, capsaicin cream.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: Well appearing. In the left side of the neck there is a small, soft, non-tender fullness that gurgles when pressed. No lymphadenopathy. Abdomen benign.

Barium swallow (today): saccular pouch off the posterior hypopharyngeal wall.

Assessment: Zenker (pharyngoesophageal) diverticulum, symptomatic.
Plan: Referral to ENT to discuss transoral endoscopic versus open repair. Upper endoscopy not needed before that consultation. Soft diet, small bites, remain upright after eating.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: ENT consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology - head and neck surgery
Date of visit: 07/20/2022
Re: Eugene Connolly, DOB 09/09/1954

Kindly referred by gastroenterology for a symptomatic pharyngoesophageal diverticulum seen on barium swallow last month. Ongoing dysphagia, nightly regurgitation with cough, halitosis.

Allergies: no known drug allergies. On warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

Exam: oral cavity and oropharynx normal. Flexible laryngoscopy: pooled secretions in the hypopharynx, vocal folds mobile, no mass. Neck: soft left-sided fullness. Good neck extension and mouth opening for transoral access.

Plan: transoral endoscopic stapling of the diverticulum under general anesthesia with an overnight stay. Warfarin to be held 5 days before; given his stroke risk profile, no bridging needed per our usual practice, coordinated with his primary care office. Scheduled 08/24/2022.

documents.title: Operative note and discharge
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside hospital - otolaryngology
Admitted 08/24/2022, discharged 08/25/2022
Procedure: transoral endoscopic stapled diverticulotomy for pharyngoesophageal diverticulum.
Anesthesia: general. Findings: posterior pharyngeal pouch with a well-defined common wall, divided completely with an endoscopic stapler. No perforation. Minimal blood loss.
Warfarin held 5 days preoperatively.
Allergies: NKDA.
Postop course: comfortable overnight, no fever, no neck swelling or crepitus. Clear liquids this morning without difficulty.
Discharge plan: full liquids 2 days then soft diet for a week. Resume warfarin tonight at his usual 5 mg. INR check next week with primary care. Follow-up ENT in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Emergency eye visit
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department - ophthalmology on call
Visit 01/25/2023
Patient: Eugene Connolly, 68-year-old man

CC: right eye pain, vision worse x2 days.

HPI: Four weeks after uncomplicated right cataract surgery. Two days ago the right eye became suddenly painful with blurred vision, and both have steadily worsened. Has diabetes (with foot neuropathy), past nasal skin cancer and a swallowing pouch treated last year.

Meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, warfarin, atorvastatin. Allergies: none known.

Exam: Right upper lid swollen. Conjunctiva diffusely injected. Slit lamp: corneal edema, hypopyon, marked anterior chamber and vitreous inflammation. VA right hand motions, left 20/30. Fundus view poor through the corneal edema. B-scan: vitreous opacities, retina attached.

Assessment: acute postoperative endophthalmitis, right eye.

Treatment: vitreous tap with intravitreal vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL and ceftazidime 2.25 mg/0.1 mL. Sample to microbiology. Moxifloxacin drops four times daily and prednisolone acetate 1% hourly while awake. Warfarin continued.
Follow-up: retina clinic in 48 hours.

Addendum 01/28: vitreous culture growing coagulase-negative staphylococci, covered by intravitreal vancomycin.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology practice
Date of visit: 11/02/2023
Re: Eugene Connolly, 69 M

Referred for two to three months of exertional fatigue without chest discomfort. Risk factors: type 2 diabetes about 17 years, hypertension, former smoker 20 pack-years, father with MI at 72. Chronic atrial fibrillation on warfarin.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, warfarin, atorvastatin 40. Allergies: none.
Exam: irregularly irregular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: atrial fibrillation, rate controlled, no ischemic changes.
Impression: exertional fatigue, possible ischemic equivalent in a diabetic. AF with resting ventricular rates in the 70s.
Plan: pharmacologic (regadenoson) nuclear perfusion study, since AF makes exercise ECG less interpretable. Will see him back with results.

reports.text:
PROTOCOL: Rest and regadenoson stress Tc-99m sestamibi SPECT with gating.
STRESS: Regadenoson 0.4 mg IV. Mild flushing. No chest pain. Rhythm atrial fibrillation throughout; no ischemic ST changes on the stress ECG.
IMAGES: Small, mild reversible defect of the inferior wall. Remaining walls with normal perfusion. Gated images: normal wall motion, LVEF 56%. Normal LV size.
reports.conclusion: Small reversible inferior perfusion defect; LVEF 56%. Positive study. Coronary angiography recommended.

events.reason: Scheduled coronary angiography after positive stress test

reports.text:
INDICATION: Positive pharmacologic nuclear study (small reversible inferior defect) with exertional fatigue.
ACCESS: Right radial artery, 6 Fr sheath. Warfarin continued, INR 2.1.
CONTRAST: iodinated contrast, low volume given creatinine 1.5; IV fluids before and after.
FINDINGS: Left main normal. LAD, circumflex and right coronary artery without angiographic disease. Right dominant system.
EVENT: During exchange of the peripheral IV tubing in the left forearm, air entered the venous line. Patient developed sudden cough and brief dyspnea; SpO2 fell to 88%; blood pressure maintained. Placed left side down, head low, on 100% oxygen. Symptoms settled within 10 minutes. Bedside echocardiogram showed microbubbles in the right heart that cleared on repeat images. Neurological exam normal.
HEMOSTASIS: radial band.
reports.conclusion: No angiographic coronary artery disease; nuclear inferior defect consistent with diaphragmatic attenuation. Venous air embolism via peripheral IV, resolved with positioning and oxygen.

documents.title: Cardiac catheterization and overnight observation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside hospital - cardiology
Admitted 12/12/2023 for elective coronary angiography, discharged 12/13/2023.

69-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, chronic atrial fibrillation and prior diabetic neuropathy and pharyngeal pouch repair, referred after a positive regadenoson study. No chest pain; occasional tiredness with exertion. Says he is passing urine normally. No known kidney disease.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, warfarin, atorvastatin. Allergies: NKDA.
Pre-procedure: BP 128/76, HR 76. Creatinine 1.5.
Because of the creatinine and the need for iodinated contrast: IV hydration, minimized contrast, metformin held for 48 hours.

Result: no coronary artery disease. The perfusion defect is attributed to attenuation.
Complication: venous air embolism from the peripheral IV during a tubing exchange - transient cough, dyspnea and desaturation to 88%, treated with left lateral head-down positioning and 100% oxygen, resolved within 10 minutes; echo microbubbles cleared; no neurological deficit. Observed overnight on telemetry without further events.
Morning creatinine 1.4.

Discharge: resume metformin 12/14, 48 hours after contrast. Please check a BMP within the week. Continue all other medications. No cardiology follow-up needed for coronary disease.

documents.title: Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cath records reviewed: clean coronaries, brief air embolism from the IV line that resolved during the case. Creatinine 1.1 today, back to his usual - the 1.5 before the cath doesn't fit his other values. He restarted metformin 12/14 as cardiology instructed; fine to continue. Pt informed, feels well, no shortness of breath.
